headline: SCOTTIE HITS 120 g/t GOLD OVER 1.5m AT BLUEBERRY — 2026 Final Assays Return 25.5 g/t Over 14m; BC Golden Triangle Vein System Keeps Delivering
snippet: Scottie Resources (TSX-V: SCOT) reported a 14-metre intercept averaging 25.5 g/t gold at the Blueberry Contact Zone within its Scottie Gold Mine in British Columbia's Golden Triangle, with a 1.5-metre sub-interval returning 120 g/t gold — headline results from the company's 61,578-metre, 227-hole 2026 drill program now entering its final assay release phase. For junior mining investors, the Blueberry Contact Zone has consistently delivered high-grade gold over more than 1.45 kilometres of defined strike, and a 14-metre interval at 25.5 g/t adds material scale context to what was initially characterised as a narrow vein-style deposit; the 120 g/t sub-interval signals a bonanza-grade kernel within a broader mineralised envelope that is still open along strike and at depth.

headline: TRUMP: US WILL 'CATCH CHINA' ON RARE EARTHS IN 10 MONTHS — USAR Rises 5%, MP Materials Gains 3% as White House Pledge Splits Sector Winners From Laggards
snippet: President Trump stated on November 19 that the US is producing rare earths 'at a level it has never reached' and will close the gap with China within 10 months, triggering a split reaction in the sector: USA Rare Earth (USAR) gained 5% and MP Materials (MP) added 3%, while Critical Metals dipped on doubts about feedstock security. The pledge comes the day after APEC-week US-China rare earth talks sent sector names 7-8% higher — two consecutive White House signals in 48 hours are adding durability to the rare earth recovery thesis, though the question of whether 10 months is a credible timeline is driving differentiation between investors backing domestic producers and those skeptical of execution timelines against China's 60%-plus share of global separation capacity.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $3,715 AS HAWKISH FED MINUTES AND IRAN RISK SQUEEZE RECOVERY — Dollar Strengthens on Two Fronts; Key Floor Now $3,650
snippet: Spot gold stabilised near $3,715 Thursday after Wednesday's hawkish Federal Reserve minutes reinforced a December rate hike at approximately 90% probability, while simultaneously escalating Iran tensions are strengthening the US dollar as a safe-haven currency — a rare scenario in which geopolitical risk lifts the dollar instead of gold, keeping precious metals under dual pressure. USA Gold's daily market report notes that the market is caught between the fundamental long-term demand case for metals and financial conditions that continue to favour the dollar; key support sits at $3,650, with a break of that level flagged by multiple analysts as the trigger for a move toward the $3,500 zone — the deep-value accumulation level where central bank buyers are expected to step in.

headline: EU THREATENS TO BLOCK MMG'S $500M ANGLO AMERICAN NICKEL DEAL — Dec 21 Decision Could Set Precedent for Chinese Acquisitions of Overseas Resources
snippet: European Union regulators are preparing to block MMG Ltd's $500 million acquisition of Anglo American's Brazilian ferronickel assets, citing concerns that European stainless steel producers would lose a critical supply source, with a binding EU decision expected by December 21 that mining legal experts describe as a potential landmark ruling on Chinese state-linked acquisitions of strategic overseas resources. MMG has countered with long-term supply commitment offers rather than structural divestiture, but the EU considers behavioural remedies insufficient; the Brazilian competition authority and the American Iron and Steel Institute have launched parallel objections, creating a three-jurisdiction approval wall for a deal that China Signal's November 19 newsletter says could establish a durable precedent affecting future Chinese resource-sector M&A globally.

headline: RIO TINTO CEO AT APEC: MORE COPPER NEEDED BY 2050 THAN MINED SINCE THE PHOENICIANS — 'Historic Demand' Cited While Financial Market Sells LME to 7-Month Lows
snippet: Rio Tinto CEO Jakob Stausholm told leaders at the APEC CEO Summit that the world will require more copper between now and 2050 than has been mined in all of recorded human history since ancient Phoenicia, urging greater supply-chain cooperation between mining nations and technology manufacturers to avoid a structural supply crisis. The statement lands as LME copper trades near seven-month lows on AI demand fears and dollar strength — reinforcing the structural demand argument that physical copper traders made at Asia Copper Week while the futures market tells a different story; for retail investors evaluating copper producer exposure, Stausholm's framing encapsulates why physical copper import premiums in China remain near record levels even as financial copper sells off.

headline: GOLDSEEK SWOT: BARRICK'S NORTH AMERICAN GOLD IPO NEARING YEAR-END — Nevada-Dominican Assets Spinoff Called Catalyst for Undervalued ABX Shares
snippet: GoldSeek's US Global Investors SWOT column highlights Barrick Mining's planned US IPO of its North American gold assets — including Nevada Gold Mines and Pueblo Viejo in the Dominican Republic — as this week's most significant sector development, with Jefferies analysts having called the year-end IPO target a potential re-rating catalyst for Barrick shares now trading more than 30% below their August peak. The subsidiary, targeting a 15-20% minority stake listed on the NYSE at an estimated entity value near $60 billion, would create the largest pure-play North American gold vehicle available to US institutional investors — a structural demand driver for the shares at a moment when generalist capital is otherwise exiting the sector; Barrick said the IPO remains subject to market conditions and final board approval.

headline: LYNAS UP 3.84% AS ASX MATERIALS SECTOR TUMBLES — World's Largest Non-Chinese Rare Earth Producer Bucks Broad Mining Selloff
snippet: Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC) gained 3.84% to A$12.845 while the broader ASX materials sector fell sharply, making it one of the standout outperformers in an otherwise brutal session for Australian mining equities — a move attributed to the APEC-week US-China rare earth negotiations and Trump's latest supply-chain pledge that lifted US-listed peers overnight. As the world's only significant rare earth producer operating outside Chinese state ownership, Lynas sits at the intersection of geopolitical supply-chain diversification and rare earth recovery narratives; a session where most miners sold off while Lynas held up is consistent with institutional sector rotation into supply-chain critical assets rather than broad-based precious metals buying.

headline: MONTEORO MINERALS DEBUTS ON TSX-V, HIGHLIGHTS MULTIPLE COLOMBIA GOLD-COPPER TARGETS — La Ruana Project Covers Porphyry and Epithermal Systems
snippet: Monteoro Minerals (TSX-V: MTAU) listed on the TSX Venture Exchange and highlighted multiple gold and copper targets at its La Ruana project in Colombia — a jurisdiction that has produced multi-million-ounce discoveries for companies including Collective Mining and Aris Mining over the past decade. La Ruana's combination of porphyry copper-gold and epithermal gold-silver target types offers parallel exploration vectors in a region where infrastructure is improving and permitting timelines are shortening; for investors evaluating new TSX-V listings, the company enters the market at a stage where initial drill targeting work is underway, making it a high-risk/high-reward speculative position rather than a near-resource story.

headline: FXSTREET: SILVER AND MINERS FALL HARDER WHEN STOCKS BREAK — Nov 17 Analysis Sees No Base Yet; Cautions Against Premature Long Entries
snippet: FXStreet's November 17 technical analysis identifies a consistent pattern in the current correction: when equity markets experience broad sell sessions, silver and junior gold miners fall proportionally harder than gold — a dynamic reflecting their status as leveraged risk assets rather than pure inflation hedges in a rising-rate environment. The analysis describes the current move as 'another verification of the breakdown to new 2026 lows' and argues that the sector's base formation has not yet completed, cautioning against premature long entries before RSI bottoms and reverses rather than simply touches oversold territory — a distinction the piece says separates historically successful dip-buyers from those who bought the first bounce rather than the actual floor.

headline: INVESTING.COM: GOLD INVESTORS EYE $3,500 AS DEEP-VALUE ZONE — Breakout Odds Improving if December Fed Hike Is Already Priced In
snippet: An Investing.com analysis argues that long-term gold investors are identifying the $3,400-$3,500 zone as a generational accumulation level, based on the confluence of central bank buying floors, historical bull-market retracement levels, and the structural disconnect between financial and physical gold demand that has persisted through the current correction. The piece frames December's FOMC meeting as the decisive near-term catalyst: if the market's current 90%-plus probability of a rate hike is correctly priced, the sell-on-confirmation dynamic that typically follows an already-priced event could mark the actual correction low — making the $3,500 zone a potentially de-risked entry for investors who have waited out the selloff.
